correctness.rationale: For every finite field of characteristic greater than 3, character orthogonality turns the fourth moment into exact pair-sum fibers. The quartic-sum identity factors as (P-Q)(P+Q-2s^2), and a quadratic-character sum with discriminant -96 gives w(0)=3q-2+(q-1)chi(-7), w(t)=3q-3-chi(-7)-2chi(-3) for nonzero t. A fully enumerated zero-count stratification yields the exact polynomial for every complex origin coefficient. Differentiation, Descartes uniqueness of the positive critical root, and monotonicity in the nonsquare regime give the sharp invariant-subspace norm and equality cases. The linear characteristic-seven case is explicitly handled. Separate symbolic derivative identities passed and the embedded finite-field Gaussian-integer fiber checker passed for 14 fields, including quadratic extensions; finite tests only corroborate the universal proof. The norm of the unrestricted operator is not claimed.

value.rationale: The multiplicative reparametrization group of the quartic graph has a canonical fixed input subspace, so computing its exact fourth-moment operator norm is a natural symmetry-controlled lower bound for the unrestricted restriction problem. The optimal coefficient has a field-arithmetic phase transition dictated by chi(-7), distinct from the earlier chi(-3) total-energy split; it vanishes at the origin for nonsquares, is strictly enhanced for squares or characteristic seven, and is unique up to scalar. A nonzero explicit first variation at the constant function excludes a natural full-space candidate for every odd characteristic greater than three. These exact invariant and stationarity facts guide future sharp Fourier extension work, without claiming a full operator norm or major downstream theorem.
